# bugs #2893: Warning about an empty translation unit before the syntax error when the first token of a file is invalid

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2893/
- Category: [Analyzed, not fixed](../../unresolved.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Keep open. r13845 changed the wording of the warning and not the condition for it.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176 a source file whose first token is `;` gets two messages. The first is
`warning 190: ISO C forbids an empty translation unit`, and the second is the syntax error for the
semicolon. The file is not empty, so the warning is wrong. Declarations after the semicolon do not
change the result, and a file that starts with `}` gets the same warning before its syntax error.

This was reproduced for mcs51 with the default standard, with `--std-c99`, with `--std-c23`, and
with `--model-large --stack-auto`, and for z80. An empty file and a file that contains only a
`#define` get the warning alone, which is correct. A file with a declaration and a `;` on the next
line gets only the syntax error.

## Known

The rule `file` in `src/SDCC.y` has an empty alternative, and its action calls
`werror (W_EMPTY_TRANSLATION_UNIT)`. In the parser that bison generates, this alternative is the
default reduction of the initial state. The parser reduces by it, and runs the action, for every
first token that cannot begin an external declaration. It reports the syntax error afterwards.

[r13845](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/13845/), which a maintainer names in the ticket's
comment, renamed the warning from "empty source file" to "empty translation unit". It did not
change the rule.

The syntax error is correct, as the reporter says. The grammar of C11 6.7 and 6.9 has no
declaration that consists of a semicolon alone.

## Open

The warning has to be given only when the input ends before any external declaration. The parser
reads the lookahead token before it reduces in the initial state, so the action of the empty
alternative can compare that token with the end of input. The warning can also be given after
`yyparse` returns. Neither was tried.
